subject: Third-Party Electric Supply Consumer Protection
overview: The Massachusetts Attorney General's Office presented on the risks of competitive electric supply and the benefits of municipal aggregation. The presentation detailed deceptive marketing practices and shared data on significant financial losses experienced by residents enrolled with third-party suppliers.

items.title: Overview of Electric Supply Options
items.summary: Sierra Mall defined the supply and delivery components of electric bills and compared the three primary sourcing options available to residents: basic service, municipal aggregation, and third-party suppliers.

items.title: Medford Community Electricity Comparison
items.summary: Mall presented Medford's municipal aggregation rates, noting they are currently lower than National Grid's basic service and offer more price stability than third-party teaser offers.

items.title: Risks of Competitive Supply Contracts
items.summary: The presentation highlighted common contract pitfalls including introductory teaser rates that transition to high variable prices, automatic renewals, and steep cancellation fees.

items.title: Sales Tactics and Consumer Protection
items.summary: Mall warned against aggressive sales representatives impersonating utility workers and advised residents to never share utility account numbers with unsolicited callers or door-to-door solicitors.

items.title: Financial Impact and Low-Income Data
items.summary: Data from the Attorney General’s Office showed Massachusetts residents lost over $651 million to third-party suppliers over nine years, with low-income Medford households experiencing a disproportionate financial burden.

items.title: Attorney General's Office Resources
items.summary: Mall outlined the office's investigative work into deceptive suppliers and provided instructions for residents to file formal consumer complaints.
